findings.title: Failed items are still marked complete and committed
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run() calls offset_tracker.complete_offset() in a finally block even when result_processor raises. ResultProcessor.__call__ also swallows exceptions internally and returns normally. In both cases the offset becomes committable and _commit_loop will commit it. A poison or transiently failing result is therefore acked with no retry, DLQ, or requeue, causing silent data loss.

findings.title: Strategy close shuts down shared queue pool breaking rebalances
findings.body: FixedQueuePool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and shared across all strategies returned by create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/terminate()/join() call queue_pool.shutdown(). On Kafka rebalance Arroyo closes the old strategy, which shuts down workers and queues still referenced by the new strategy. Subsequent submits go to shut-down queues and workers never process again.

findings.title: Commit scan iterates over offset number range and leaks memory on stall
findings.body: OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets() does for offset in range(start, max_offset+1) where start/max are Kafka offsets. A gap from a stalled head-of-line item or a large log jump makes this loop iterate millions of integers every second in _commit_loop. Meanwhile all_offsets only shrinks on mark_committed, so if offset N never completes all later offsets accumulate unbounded in two sets, growing memory until the stall clears.

findings.title: Partition lock map accessed without synchronization
findings.body: OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock() reads and mutates self.partition_locks dict with get/setdefault and no global lock, while add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable_offsets/mark_committed can run concurrently from submit, worker threads, and commit thread. Concurrent creation for a new Partition can create duplicate Lock objects or raise, so two threads can then guard the same partition with different locks and corrupt all_offsets/outstanding.

findings.title: wait_until_empty ignores in-flight items
findings.body: wait_until_empty() and get_stats() use only queue.qsize(). An item already removed from the queue by a worker but not yet processed and completed via complete_offset() is invisible, so the function can return True while work is still in flight. Any caller using it as a drain barrier will proceed prematurely.
